research_goal: Test whether compost mulch improves early dry-season soil moisture.
protocol: Randomized comparison of 20 trees with 5 cm compost mulch and 20 unmulched trees for 8 weeks.
result: Mulched trees had 12% more cherries at the final count and visibly less midday wilt.
change_from_previous: Baseline; no prior mulch trial in this block.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Directly tests the project's initial soil-moisture hypothesis.

research_goal: Repeat the compost mulch comparison under heavier shade.
protocol: Matched 20-tree comparison with 5 cm compost mulch under approximately 70% shade for 8 weeks.
result: No yield improvement; six mulched trees showed fungal leaf spots after prolonged wet mornings.
failure_mode: Excess moisture and fungal leaf spots under high shade.
change_from_previous: Increased shade from 40% to 70% while keeping mulch depth at 5 cm.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; conflicting follow-up, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: A direct conflicting replication that changes how the project prioritizes mulch and shade trials.

research_goal: Compare shallow and deep mulch during a dry spell.
protocol: Three arms of 18 trees each: no mulch, 3 cm mulch, and 8 cm mulch; observations for 6 weeks.
result: The 3 cm arm had the highest cherry retention; the 8 cm arm was similar to control.
change_from_previous: Added a 3 cm arm and fixed supplemental irrigation at 2 liters per tree per week.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; modest and short-duration result, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Tests a concrete condition range needed to interpret the first mulch result.

research_goal: Test moderate shade reduction for flowering consistency.
protocol: Prune shade trees to target 35% versus an unpruned 55% shade control; 24 trees per arm.
result: The 35% shade arm produced 9% more flowers, but the harvest count was inconclusive.
change_from_previous: Reduced shade target from approximately 55% to 35%.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; flowering is not the same as yield, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Explores a plausible shade lever, but the missing harvest endpoint limits project decisions.

research_goal: Check whether aggressive shade reduction increases yield.
protocol: Compare 15% shade with 35% shade for one flowering cycle; 16 trees per arm.
result: Leaves showed heat stress and berry count was 6% lower than the 35% shade comparison.
failure_mode: Heat stress after aggressive shade reduction.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: A high-risk boundary condition that helps prevent repeating an aggressive shade change.

research_goal: Compare compost tea concentrations for cherry retention.
protocol: Weekly foliar applications at 0%, 2%, and 5% concentration, randomized across 30 trees for 5 weeks.
result: The 2% arm retained 8% more cherries than control; the 5% arm was not better.
change_from_previous: Introduced a concentration series instead of a single treatment.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Tests a separate treatment family and supplies a concentration comparison for future trials.

research_goal: Repeat the 2% compost tea treatment in a wetter site.
protocol: 2% weekly foliar application versus water control across 24 trees for 4 weeks.
result: No measurable retention difference; untreated controls had slightly more retained cherries.
failure_mode: Cold, wet conditions and short observation window.
change_from_previous: Moved from 45% shade with weekly irrigation to 60% shade without irrigation.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; insufficient replication, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: A failed replication that is important for identifying site and weather dependence.

research_goal: Test regulated deficit irrigation during fruit filling.
protocol: Compare 4 liters weekly with 2 liters weekly for 10 weeks, 25 trees per arm.
result: The 4-liter arm had 11% higher mean cherry mass; confidence was limited because blocks were uneven.
change_from_previous: Increased irrigation from 2 to 4 liters per tree per week while retaining 3 cm mulch.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; limited block balance, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Directly informs the project's irrigation decision, despite weak block balance.

research_goal: Test whether more irrigation always improves cherry mass.
protocol: Compare 4 liters and 8 liters weekly for 8 weeks with 3 cm mulch; 20 trees per arm.
result: The 8-liter arm had more yellowing leaves and no additional cherry mass over 4 liters.
failure_mode: Possible overwatering; soil drainage was not measured.
change_from_previous: Increased irrigation from 4 to 8 liters per tree per week.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; drainage was unmeasured, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: A high-priority boundary test for whether more water should be avoided, even though it failed.

research_goal: Compare hand weeding frequency for flowering and yield.
protocol: Monthly weeding versus biweekly weeding across 30 trees for one season.
result: Biweekly weeding was associated with 7% more flowers, but harvest data were not collected.
change_from_previous: Shortened weeding interval from 30 to 14 days.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; missing harvest endpoint, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Explores labor intensity but cannot resolve the project's yield question without harvest data.

research_goal: Investigate a suspected wilt and low-yield problem.
protocol: Compare affected and unaffected rows; record soil moisture, shade, symptoms, and cherry count for 3 weeks.
result: Affected rows had wilt, standing water after rain, and 22% fewer cherries than unaffected rows.
failure_mode: Waterlogging suspected; no pathogen test was performed.
change_from_previous: Added symptom and drainage observations instead of changing one treatment variable.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; diagnosis is incomplete, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Directly matches the current wilt and low-yield problem and changes the next diagnostic step.

research_goal: Test drainage channels for the suspected wilt problem.
protocol: Install shallow drainage channels in 12 affected trees and compare with 12 affected controls for 6 weeks.
result: Wilt symptoms decreased in the channel group, but cherry recovery was not measured to harvest.
change_from_previous: Reduced shade and mulch and added drainage channels after the waterlogging observation.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; symptom result without harvest endpoint, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: Tests a targeted response to the highest-priority current problem, although harvest impact is unknown.

research_goal: Assess whether pruning improves airflow and reduces leaf disease.
protocol: Selective pruning versus routine pruning in 18-tree blocks; monitor leaf spots for 5 weeks.
result: Leaf spots were lower after selective pruning, but yield was not measured and blocks differed in age.
failure_mode: Confounding by block age and missing yield endpoint.
change_from_previous: Changed pruning pattern while leaving shade target nominally similar.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; insufficient for yield conclusions, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: May inform disease follow-up, but confounding prevents a direct yield decision.

research_goal: Compare mulched and unmulched trees for a current low-yield complaint.
protocol: Pair 15 trees by slope position, then assign 3 cm mulch or no mulch; measure cherries for 10 weeks.
result: Mulched trees had 10% higher cherry count, but the estimate overlapped zero across paired blocks.
change_from_previous: Added paired assignment and slope matching to reduce location imbalance.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; uncertain estimate, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: A close replication of the current low-yield question with improved pairing, despite uncertainty.

research_goal: Replicate the 3 cm mulch result with a harvest endpoint.
protocol: Three matched blocks of 20 trees each: 0 cm, 3 cm, and 6 cm mulch; measure cherry mass through harvest.
result: No clear difference at harvest; a late hail event damaged one block and reduced usable comparisons.
failure_mode: Hail damage and incomplete block comparison.
change_from_previous: Added a 6 cm arm and extended measurement through harvest.
notes: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC RECORD; inconclusive replication, not a real agricultural finding or farming advice.
impact_reason: A failed harvest-endpoint replication that strongly affects whether the mulch line should continue.
